manual_findings.finding: Exact tuple pair records and exact prior integer child references make structural values well-founded. Rejecting duplicate ordered reference pairs makes representation injective by induction on maximum structural height. Atoms and pairs are disjoint.

Every source node has an actual target pair image; every image is distinct; both child equations are checked for every source pair. Atoms map identically by definition. The declared seed prefix is compared record-by-record and must have the identity image. No source node is replaced by a selected subset.

If the target contains every source structural value, uniqueness provides the embedding. Appending canonical nodes preserves old values and old images; canonical cons either reuses a pair or extends the embedding. The inclusion premise is explicit and is not established for the real initialized machine by this Source.

The finite checker inspects active function/PC, every register and every bottom-to-top saved frame, including saved function/continuation/destination and every register. Exact shapes are externally attributed to the same program. One-past-end PC is a related nonfetchable state, not an acceptance claim.

The manual covers const/move/cons/head/tail/pair/atom/succ/not/branch/jump/call/return. It agrees with the pinned abstract tree VM: operands precede destination writes, pair-kind is preserved, atom equality includes nil but excludes pairs, succ requires a byte below 255, Boolean operations require 0/1, CALL saves advanced PC/all caller registers and reads all arguments before rewrite, root return accepts exactly 1.

Under the same validated immutable program, complete initial structural inclusion/state relation, correct abstract opcode semantics and finite successful administrative work, induction on a finite valid execution preserves the relation and root decision. This is a defensible conditional manual theorem. It is not an all-input status/cost equivalence or physical macro-step proof.

The checker uses exact int/tuple tests for reference/control/state carriers; booleans and subclasses are not references. Invalid mapping/shape/vector/frame paths refuse. Heap dictionaries hash only flat exact pairs of integer references; this Source does not construct recursive native value tuples as hash keys.

The entry holds full raw input owners and actual Work before start invokes the Root callback. Work calls genuine Root before private limit classification. Public exceptions default owner=None; genuine owned raises supply the private owner. Foreign exceptions are reraised without replacement and attachment is best-effort. This remains a nonhostile/read-only callback baseline, not a security sandbox.

proof: Prior references make the child relation well founded.
Define a structural value for each atom and then for each ordered pair, in increasing node order.
manual_sections.statement: Let \(A=\{0,\ldots,256\}\). A finite heap \(H\) has node references \(257+i\), with record \(H_i=(a_i,b_i)\) satisfying \(a_i,b_i<257+i\). Distinct node records have distinct ordered child-reference pairs. The atom \(256\) is nil.
manual_sections.title: Canonical value heaps

proof: Atoms and constructed pairs have disjoint value forms; different atoms have different values.
For two pairs with equal structural values, their corresponding children have equal structural values. Induction on the maximum structural height makes both child references equal.
Canonical uniqueness of the ordered child-reference pair then makes the two parent references equal. This covers every finite structural height.
manual_sections.title: Lemma: each value has one reference

proof: Define \(e_{H,K}(r)\) to be the unique reference in \(K\) with value \(\nu_H(r)\). Existence is the stated inclusion assumption; uniqueness is the preceding lemma.
The map fixes atoms because atom and pair values are disjoint. If two images agree, their source values agree, so source references agree.
For a source pair, the target representative has exactly the images of its two children: applying \(\nu_K\) to both children and using injectivity proves the two reference equalities.
manual_sections.statement: Let \(K\) be another canonical heap containing a structural representative of every value represented in \(H\). There is a unique injective map \(e_{H,K}\) preserving every value, fixing atoms and commuting with both children.
manual_sections.title: Lemma: extra nodes preserve values

proof: Appending prior-reference nodes cannot change any earlier structural value.
An existing target representative keeps its reference; canonical uniqueness prevents a later distinct representative of that value.
Therefore any extended embedding \(e^+\) satisfies \(e^+|_H=e\). Extra program metadata and captured argument-list nodes may be inserted in the target heap.
manual_sections.statement: If canonical heaps \(H\) and \(K\) extend without modifying existing records, the value-preserving embedding of old references does not change.
manual_sections.title: Lemma: appending metadata keeps old images

proof: If the source pair already exists, its image is the unique target representative with those image children.
If it is new in the source, add it there. The target either reuses its existing pair or adds a fresh pair with the corresponding children.

In either case the heaps remain canonical, previous images remain fixed, and the embedding extends by exactly the source result when necessary. No equal allocation count or result identifier is required.
manual_sections.statement: Given corresponding child references, canonical pair construction produces corresponding results. The target may already contain the pair as metadata or a cached argument list.
manual_sections.title: Lemma: canonical pair construction commutes

proof: Active function and next instruction indices must be identical; both complete register vectors have the declared register count.
Every target register contains \(e\) of its source value.
The complete bottom-to-top frame sequences have equal length. Corresponding saved functions, return instructions and destinations agree, and every saved register value corresponds under \(e\).
The target may contain extra heap nodes, but those nodes are not additional program instructions, axioms or certificate choices.
manual_sections.statement: For the same valid immutable program, relate active function index, next instruction index, complete register vector and every saved caller frame. Functions, instruction indices and destinations are control data; the embedding acts on value references.
manual_sections.title: Complete machine-state relation

proof: Proceed by induction on the number of executed instructions. The base is the complete initial relation, which must be supplied rather than inferred from a matching root identifier.
Both sides fetch the same instruction and advance the next-instruction counter before executing it. Apply the exhaustive opcode cases below.

Canonical pair construction extends the embedding; every other value operation preserves it. Frame operations preserve the complete relation, including aliases, repeated arguments and untouched registers.
Administrative extra allocation is finite and canonical and cannot change an earlier value. It therefore preserves the relation between instruction boundaries.
At a root return, acceptance is exactly return value \(1\). The embedding fixes \(1\) and is injective, so both decisions agree. A nonaccepting stuck fetch is not converted into acceptance.
manual_sections.statement: Assume the same validated immutable program, corresponding initial heaps/input states, correct abstract opcode semantics and finite successful administrative work between instruction boundaries. Ignore resource cutoffs. Then every finite valid opcode execution has a corresponding execution under canonical extra-node allocation, preserving the complete state relation and the root acceptance decision.
manual_sections.title: Conditional abstract-machine simulation theorem

proof: It does not prove that the physical tape controller implements each abstract transition; that requires a complete macro-step refinement and decoding argument.
It does not prove that a Wang tiling is an initialized accepting tape history; the full initializer and spacetime construction need their own proof.
It does not establish full compiled common-checker image attribution, exact public theory/goal licensing, or native-string/raw-JSON correspondence.
It does not preserve physical heap size, allocation counts, running time, budgets or all error statuses. A fixed finite region may run out of capacity on one representation.
The old generic host fetch can raise outside its data-operation handler. The theorem concerns valid finite executions and root acceptance, not equality of all failure trajectories.
The finite certificate checker checks complete immutable heap and decoded-state relations only. It validates neither a transition nor the origin of the decoded state.
There has been no checker call, generated tile table, new actual, proof-search run, learned marking or RL training in this milestone.
manual_sections.statement: This is a manual conditional mathematical argument about abstract machines, not a theorem discovered by GCTS or RL.
manual_sections.title: What this theorem does not establish

all13_opcode_cases.argument: Constants are the same exact original seed values, so their embeddings are the same fixed seed references. Write only the selected destination.
all13_opcode_cases.name: const

all13_opcode_cases.argument: Reading a source register and copying its value commutes with \(e\), including a destination that aliases the source.
all13_opcode_cases.name: move

all13_opcode_cases.argument: Both source operands are read before the destination write. Apply the canonical-construction lemma and preserve the other registers.
all13_opcode_cases.name: cons

all13_opcode_cases.argument: Pair/atom kind is preserved. For a pair, the target left child is the image of the source left child; atom inputs fail nonacceptingly.
all13_opcode_cases.name: head

all13_opcode_cases.argument: The right-child equation gives the same argument for tail. No numeric pair identifier is observed.
all13_opcode_cases.name: tail

all13_opcode_cases.argument: Atoms \(0,\ldots,256\) stay atoms and every pair reference maps to a pair reference. The Boolean result is unchanged.
all13_opcode_cases.name: pair

all13_opcode_cases.argument: The operation tests that both operands are atoms and equal. Atoms are fixed; pairs fail the test even when their references are equal.
all13_opcode_cases.name: atom

all13_opcode_cases.argument: The operation is defined only on byte atoms \(0,\ldots,254\). These operands and their successors are fixed. Byte \(255\), nil and pair operands fail nonacceptingly.
all13_opcode_cases.name: succ

all13_opcode_cases.argument: Only exact atoms \(0\) and \(1\) are valid. They are fixed, so inversion and invalid-data decisions agree.
all13_opcode_cases.name: not

all13_opcode_cases.argument: The condition is exactly \(0\) or \(1\); both the value and the statically validated target instruction indices agree.
all13_opcode_cases.name: branch

all13_opcode_cases.argument: Both sides assign the same statically validated target instruction index; the value embedding is unaffected.
all13_opcode_cases.name: jump

all13_opcode_cases.argument: Read the full ordered caller-argument vector before replacing registers. Repeated/aliased indices correspond pointwise. Save the complete caller, already advanced return instruction and destination; initialize the same callee with corresponding arguments and nil padding. Target-only cached list nodes are administrative extra allocation.
all13_opcode_cases.name: call

all13_opcode_cases.argument: Read the result before restoring a frame. With a caller, restore every saved register and write its one saved destination. With no caller, accept exactly atom \(1\), which is preserved and reflected by the embedding.
all13_opcode_cases.name: return

whole_unrun_bank.recipe: All atoms, nil and atom/pair separation; Source booleans are rejected as integer references.
Duplicate pair, forward/negative/out-of-range child, mutable or truncated pair record.
Missing/extra image, atom image for node, nonexistent node image, duplicate image, wrong left or right child.
Incorrect declared prefix length, changed seed pair or nonidentity seed image.
Metadata before later semantic pairs, cached argument lists and reuse of already-present target pair.
Complete active register correspondence, aliases/repeated values, differing values outside the selected destination.
Changed lower frame, frame omission/reordering, changed destination/nextPC/function or an untouched saved register.
Out-of-range functions/registers, nonempty main arity, one-past-end saved continuation is a related nonaccepting state, not an accepted execution.
Reject mutable outer/inner carriers and nonexact integer subclasses; callbacks are separately owned immutable declarations.
Every private limit, first genuine Root callback failure, foreign exception identity and available raw owner/work prefixes.
A related but unreachable state pair must not become an execution or a proof-acceptance claim.
Actual tape/macro decoder, all13physical opcode refinements, fresh complete UTF8/program/body binding and full original qualification remain required.
